intro: Highlands Way North runs through the Garibaldi Highlands past a school. Residents raised concerns about speeding, especially in the school zone.
The District of Squamish put the stretch between Portree Way and Greenwood Way on its list of top traffic calming priorities for 2026.

The District says the changes were made in August 2026. The multi use lane was widened, a buffer was added between it and the travel lane, and the centre line was removed to make the road feel narrower while keeping two way traffic. A new crosswalk went in south of Pentland Way for safer trail access, and a bus stop was moved slightly south.
Because the work is already done, this question is really about whether residents support keeping these changes (as of October 2026).

timeline.what: The District planned three speed tables on Highlands Way North between The Boulevard and Portree Way. In a survey, 45% supported speed tables.
Council endorsed a new Traffic Calming Policy for Squamish.
A traffic calming request was logged for Highlands Way North, Portree Way to Pentland Way.
The stretch appeared on the District's list of eligible traffic calming locations.

points: A narrower looking road tends to slow drivers, which matters most near a school.
The wider lane and buffer give people walking and cycling more room, and the new crosswalk gives a safer way to reach the trail.
Some drivers feel the changes slow a main route in and out of the Highlands.
Removing the centre line can feel less clear to some drivers, and some would prefer a different fix, such as enforcement.

questions.q: Is this still a plan or already done?
questions.a: Done. The District says the changes were implemented in August 2026.
The District calls it a multi use lane, so it is shared by people walking and cycling. It was widened and given a buffer from traffic.

questions.q: How does the District choose streets for traffic calming?
questions.a: It looks at resident requests, then checks speed, traffic volume, collision history, the road type and emergency access. Eligible streets are ranked and the top ones are costed each year.
